entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 11 Lu 11:1-13 . Nothing of John's inner teaching (to his own disciples) has been preserved to us, but we may be sure he never taught his disciples to say, "Our Father."

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14477"/><div sID="gen28027" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14477"/><hi type="bold">27-28. as he spake these things, a ... woman of the company--</hi>of the multitude, the crowd. A charming little incident and profoundly instructive. With true womanly feeling, she envies the mother of such a wonderful Teacher. Well, and higher and better than she had said as much before her (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.28">Lu 1:28</reference>, 42); and our Lord is far from condemning it. He only holds up--as "blessed rather"--the hearers and keepers of God's word; in other words, the humblest real saint of God. (See on <reference osisRef="Matt.12.49">Mt 12:49</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.12.50">50</reference>.) How utterly alien is this sentiment from the teaching of the Church of Rome, which would excommunicate any one of its members who dared to talk in the spirit of this glorious saying! (Also see on <reference osisRef="Matt.12.43">Mt 12:43</reference>.) <div eID="gen28027" type="x-p"/>

(Also see on Mt 12:43 .)

Our Lord purposely names the most trifling products of the earth, as examples of what they punctiliously exacted the tenth of.<div eID="gen28035" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28036" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">judgment and the love of God--</hi>in <reference osisRef="Matt.23.25">Mt 23:25</reference>, "judgment, mercy, and faith." entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14486"/><div sID="gen28040" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14486"/><hi type="bold">44. appear not, &c.--</hi>As one might unconsciously walk over a grave concealed from view, and thus contract ceremonial defilement, so the plausible exterior of the Pharisees kept people from perceiving the pollution they contracted from coming in contact with such corrupt characters. (See <reference osisRef="Ps.5.9">Psa 5:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.3.13">Ro 3:13</reference>; a different illustration from <reference osisRef="Matt.23.27">Mt 23:27</reference>). <div eID="gen28040" type="x-p"/>

(See Psa 5:9 ; Ro 3:13 ; a different illustration from Mt 23:27 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14487"/><div sID="gen28041" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14487"/><hi type="bold">46. burdens grievous, &c.--</hi>referring not so much to the irksomeness of the legal rites (though they were irksome, <reference osisRef="Acts.15.10">Ac 15:10</reference>), as to the heartless rigor with which they were enforced, and by men of shameless inconsistency. <div eID="gen28041" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14488"/><div sID="gen28042" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14488"/><hi type="bold">47-48. ye build, &c.--</hi>Out of pretended respect and honor, they repaired and beautified the sepulchres of the prophets, and with whining hypocrisy said, "If we had been in the days of our fathers, we should not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets," while all the time they "were witnesses to themselves that they were the children of them that killed the prophets" (<reference osisRef="Matt.23.29">Mt 23:29</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.23.30">30</reference>); convicting themselves daily of as exact a resemblance in spirit and character to the very classes over whose deeds they pretended to mourn, as child to parent. <div eID="gen28042" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14489"/><div sID="gen28043" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14489"/><hi type="bold">49-51. said the wisdom, &c.--</hi>a remarkable variation of the words in <reference osisRef="Matt.23.34">Mt 23:34</reference>, "Behold I SEND." As there seems plainly an allusion to ancient warnings of what God would do with so incorrigible a people, so here Christ, stepping majestically into the place of God, so to speak, says, "Now I am going to carry all that out." Could this be other than the Lord of Israel in the flesh? <div eID="gen28043" type="x-p"/>

In <reference osisRef="Matt.23.13">Mt 23:13</reference>, they are accused of shutting heaven; here of taking away the key, which was worse. A right knowledge of God's Word is eternal life (<reference osisRef="John.17.3">Joh 17:3</reference>); but this they took away from the people, substituting for it their wretched traditions. <div eID="gen28047" type="x-p"/>
